locator.title: Наливной пол трескается и пылит? В чем может быть ошибка
locator.lead: Разбираем ошибки при заливке наливного пола, которые часто приводят к проблемам

nearest_text_before.text: Проблема: работа с перерывами, медленное нанесение. (Заливка должна выполняться не более с 10-15 минутами разницы между партиями). Если заливка идет частями, появляются трещины из-за неравномерного затвердевания. Как только раствор начнет схватываться, его уже невозможно выровнять.

nearest_text_after.text: Решение: залить поверхность в один заход без перерывов. Схватывание должно происходить одновременно по всему периметру.

image_reading: A dusty unfinished interior contains a large broken floor section with deep cracks, loose rubble and a raised slab fragment in the foreground.
An unattended powered demolition tool lies in the middle distance, with additional hand tools near the lower and right edges; no person or active tool contact is visible.
The foreground tools, central broken slab and farther floor edges provide readable depth, while the cause, direction and mechanics of any physical action remain ambiguous.
analysis.article_context: The body image illustrates the costly consequence of slow, interrupted pouring: uneven curing can leave a severely cracked floor that must be broken out, reinforcing the adjacent recommendation to pour the whole surface continuously.

structured_intent.editorial_meaning: Emphasize that interrupted, slow pouring can culminate in extensive cracking and demolition rather than a sound continuous floor.
structured_intent.initial_state: A damaged floor is already broken into cracked sections, with a raised slab fragment, scattered rubble and several unattended tools visible in a dusty room.
structured_intent.primary_action: Move continuously through the visible depth toward the central broken floor section.
structured_intent.terminal_state: The existing central fracture and raised slab fragment are more prominent through visible parallax, while every floor fragment and tool remains stationary.
structured_intent.geometry_invariant: All cracks, slab fragments, rubble and tools retain their rigid shapes, locations and existing contacts with the floor.
structured_intent.identity_invariant: The same broken floor sections, one powered tool and the visible hand tools remain present and recognizable; nothing is added, removed or duplicated.
structured_intent.semantic_invariant: The floor remains visibly failed and under demolition, sustaining the warning about severe cracking through the last frame.
structured_intent.feasibility_assessment: The image clearly proves a static cracked floor, loose rubble, unattended tools and usable foreground-to-background depth. It does not prove active demolition, tool contact, crack propagation, pouring direction or any safe autonomous object motion, so only source-grounded camera motion is justified.

models.scene_plan: Over five seconds, begin a moderate, continuous push-in immediately toward the central raised slab and its deepest fracture. Keep the room and all tools physically static while foreground-to-background parallax remains clearly visible; ease gently near the end when the central crack occupies slightly more of the composition.
models.positive_prompt: The camera makes a steady bounded push-in toward the central cracked slab, with the nearest hand tools shifting about 7% of the frame through source-grounded parallax. The broken floor, rubble and unattended power tool retain their rigid shapes and fixed positions, ending with the deep central fracture more prominent.

models.scene_plan: Use the full five seconds for one smooth rightward lateral track focused on the raised central slab. Maintain an even pace before a soft final deceleration; source-grounded parallax separates the foreground hand tool, cracked slab and rear floor edge without revealing anything beyond the source view.
models.positive_prompt: The camera tracks gently to the right toward the raised broken slab, moving the nearest foreground tool no more than about 8% of the frame through natural parallax. All slab fragments, cracks, rubble and unattended tools remain rigid and fixed, ending with the jagged central break more clearly separated from the rear floor edge.

models.scene_plan: For four seconds, start an immediate, smooth shallow rising move aimed at the central raised fragment. Keep travel compact but perceptible, with the foreground tools shifting against the middle-distance slab; slow only at the end as the existing fracture becomes easier to read, without constructing unseen floor or moving debris.
models.positive_prompt: The camera rises slightly toward the central broken slab at normal real-time speed, shifting the nearest foreground references roughly 5–7% of the frame through source-grounded parallax. The cracked floor, rubble and tools stay rigid and fixed, ending with a clearer view into the existing fracture around the raised slab.
